question: What is the primary target group for quarantine measures?

options.B: Healthy individuals exposed to a contagious disease

explanation: Quarantine specifically restricts people who are well but have been exposed, distinguishing them from those who are actively sick. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h1)

question: Why is the incubation period the key duration for quarantine?

options.A: It marks the exact window when the pathogen becomes completely inactive.
options.B: It is the time required for complete drug clearance in the body.
options.C: It represents the standard length of hospital admission for any fever.
options.D: It allows time to observe if exposed persons develop symptoms.

explanation: Monitoring during the incubation period ensures that anyone who was infected during exposure is identified before they can spread the disease. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h1)

question: Who is the proper subject for medical isolation?

options.A: A healthy contact of a cholera patient
options.B: A nurse returning from a community outreach
options.C: A person with a confirmed infectious illness
options.D: A traveler arriving from a malaria-endemic zone

explanation: Isolation is strictly reserved for individuals who are already sick and capable of transmitting their active infection to others. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h2)

question: What separates quarantine from isolation regarding patient status?

options.A: Quarantine lasts for life, while isolation lasts for a few days.
options.B: Quarantine requires strict hospital admission, while isolation is done at home.
options.C: Quarantine is voluntary, whereas isolation is legally mandated.
options.D: Quarantine applies to exposed healthy people, while isolation applies to sick people.

explanation: The fundamental difference lies in the health status and diagnosis of the individual being separated. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h2)

question: What type of quarantine restricts an entire neighborhood or district?
explanation: Community quarantine applies broader geographic restrictions when tracking individual contacts becomes unmanageable during severe outbreaks. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h3)

question: When is facility quarantine preferred over home quarantine?

options.A: When the patient develops severe respiratory failure
options.B: When laboratory tests confirm negative infection status
options.C: When home conditions lack space to prevent household transmission
options.D: When the exposed person prefers staying in a hotel

explanation: Facility quarantine protects family members in crowded households where self-separation is practically impossible. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h3)

question: Why must staff wear PPE in quarantine areas housing asymptomatic people?

options.A: To prevent unrecognized transmission from incubating cases
options.B: To keep facility floors completely sterile at all times
options.C: To comply with fire safety regulations in public buildings
options.D: To replace the need for handwashing protocols

explanation: Asymptomatic individuals in quarantine may already be shedding the virus, making PPE essential for worker safety. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h4)

question: A nurse enters a quarantine station to drop off supplies. What is the most critical immediate action after leaving?

options.A: File an incident report with the ministry
options.C: Spray the hallway with chemical bleach
options.D: Document the temperature check in a ledger

explanation: Hand hygiene is the single most effective barrier against cross-contamination after any potential contact in an infectious environment. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h4)

question: What is a primary nursing responsibility during daily quarantine checks?

options.A: Monitoring for early signs of infection
options.B: Administering therapeutic antibiotics to all residents
options.C: Discharging residents who feel well after one day

explanation: Daily assessment catches the very first symptoms of disease, allowing rapid separation and treatment. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h5)

question: A quarantined person develops a sudden fever on day four. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Arrange immediate transition to an isolation facility
options.B: Instruct the family to bring herbal remedies from home
options.C: Document the finding and recheck temperature next week
options.D: Extend the quarantine period for another fourteen days

explanation: Developing symptoms changes the status from an exposed contact to a suspected case, requiring immediate isolation. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h5)

question: Which Nigerian statute provides the primary legal basis for quarantine enforcement?
explanation: The Quarantine Act is the foundational legislation granting Nigerian authorities the legal power to declare and enforce quarantine. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h6)

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand the legal basis of quarantine?

options.A: To prosecute family members who bring food to the facility
options.B: To balance public safety protection with respect for human rights
options.C: To bypass obtaining informed consent for all clinical procedures
options.D: To arrest individuals who refuse to take their medications

explanation: Nurses must respect lawful authority while ensuring patient dignity and ethical treatment are maintained throughout confinement. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h6)

question: How does clear patient education improve quarantine compliance?

options.A: By shortening the incubation period of the pathogen
options.B: By eliminating the need for daily temperature checks
options.C: By reducing fear and explaining the public health purpose
options.D: By threatening legal penalties for leaving the room

explanation: When people understand why restrictions exist and what to expect, compliance and cooperation improve significantly. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h7)

question: A quarantined client exhibits severe anxiety and cries constantly about missing work. What is the most appropriate nursing intervention?

options.A: Provide active listening and connect the client to counseling services
options.B: Advise the client to ignore the feelings and focus on sleeping
options.C: Discharge the client immediately to relieve work stress
options.D: Prescribe strong sedative medications without a doctor's order

explanation: Addressing mental health needs through support and counseling helps clients cope with the psychological strain of confinement. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h7)
